header: DO NOT EDIT: regenerate with `python3 proofs/verus/gen_pin_tests.py <spec>`.
Each test mirrors one [pins] row of proofs/verus/status_reads_traversal_sync.txt
`status_liveness`), not a copy of it. The proof-side witness is named in
each test's doc comment; where the source is deliberately NARROWER than the
model (a `may` arm the source refuses to call a store), the test records the
source's answer, which is the sound direction.

pins.note: Proof: may_s(test_operand()) under the flag. Source: a `test` call whose operand text carries `$?`.
Proof: may_s(getvar_q()). Source: the structural getVar("?") arm -- this witness contains no `$?` text, so only that arm can answer it.
Proof: !may_s(echo_hi()). Source: an Output of a literal reads no status.
Proof: a bare `exit` reads, `exit 0` does not (bash exits with the current status).
Proof: an_s(FnS(body, ...)) is false unless the body is analysed on its own. Source: a `local ec=$?` inside a function localises to that body; the enclosing main list is not armed by it.
Proof: may_x(Call(Capture, [Arrow([test_operand])])). Source: the Arrow arm re-enters the statement list, because `$( ... )` runs at the point of use.
Proof: an_stores(If/While/For/Case). Source: every control-flow arm clears the status before its body, so it is a definite store (the narrow reading the source documents).
Proof: !an_stores(assign_capture()) but an_stores(assign_one()). Source: a single-target assign stores unless its expression holds a command substitution (textual capture guard).
Proof: !an_stores(Asg([_], RawQ, asm=true)) and !an_stores(Asg([_, _], RawQ, asm=false)). Source: the asm label and a multi-target assign both refuse the store.

Proof: !an_stores(ExprS(Call(GrepMatches))) but an_stores(ExprS(Call(Plain))). Source: the pure-print call arms (grepMatches, pipeline, redirect, fnValue) return without writing the register; an ordinary call stores.
Proof: nested_sem(Redir([test_operand()])). Source: the Redirect arm hands its inner list to the same read-before-store rule.
Proof: !nested_sem(Redir([assign_one(), test_operand()])). Source: a definite store before the read absorbs it, so the statement needs no leading store of its own.
Proof: an_nested(CaseS(...clause bodies...)) but !an_nested(FnS(...)). Source: case clause bodies are scanned by the nested rule; a function body is its own statement list and is not.
Proof: facts_sound on assign_capture() -- !an_s, !an_stores, !nested_sem together. Source: the same three predicates on a single-target capture assign.
